doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Jingle dates with Louis Armstrong and Ella Fitzgerald
summary: Playing jingles with Armstrong and Ella, and the story of Louis and the turnaround.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When you went in to do like a studio date most of the time you didn’t know what it was for, is that correct?
So like a soap commercial or something like that, would you ever hear the final product like would the singers be there?

Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Well sometimes, in the old days they used to bring the singers in later to track, they’d sing to our track. We’d be leaving, packing up, and they’d come in and they’d put the singers on. But I mean Steve Carmen sent me — this jingle writer — he sent me a CD of all the stuff that I did with him.

Bundles of stuff. And man, we did stuff with Ella Fitzgerald, we did stuff with Satchmo, Louis Armstrong man. I mean I’m sitting there behind the drums and there’s Louis. You know? Singing about tires, Goodyear Tires or something. And Ella singing some tune swinging, all swinging stuff you know but that was a highlight for me in that business was playing with them.

Oh man it was like, there was a thing I remember there was a scene where Louis is standing there and one of the agency people is asking Louis to play a turnaround coming out of something. And Louis is just kind of like smiling, not really saying much. And the conductor is trying to talk about it and Louis is — and finally one of the guys, nobody knew what was happening and one of the guys in the band, the trombone player yells out, he says, “Hey man that’s Louis. Louis invented what you’re asking for. Just let him play.” And it was true man. He invented what the guy was asking for you know. And Louis — he was just so nice you know, he just did it. I remember certain players are just natural man, like John Bunch. Remember John Bunch?
